## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Chattamāṇavakavimānavatthu* ("The Boy Chatta’s Mansion", Vv 53) is a narrative discourse in the *Vimānavatthu* collection of the Pali canon [SuttaCentral]. The text recounts how the Buddha instructs a young boy named Chatta on taking refuge and observing the moral precepts [SuttaCentral]. In secondary scholarship on Buddhist death practices and rebirth ideology, Gregory Schopen cites story no. 53 of the *Vimānavatthu* as an instance illustrating the prominent belief in early Pali literature that an individual's mental state or disposition at the moment of death strongly determines their future fate and rebirth [Schopen 1978].

DharmaNexus identifies substantial internal Pali text reuse between Vv 53 and its commentary, the *Vimānavatthu-aṭṭhakathā* (comprising 27 matches, with the longest continuous correspondence spanning verses §9.4–17.1), alongside shared phrasing with the *Pajahanavāra* of the *Yamaka* (Ya 7.2.3) [DharmaNexus]. In cross-language alignments, DharmaNexus detects low-scoring automated matches with Tibetan texts—including the *Maitreyamahāsiṃhanādasūtra* (D0067) and the *Varṇārhavarṇa-stotra* (D1138)—as well as the Chinese *Saṃyuktāgama* (T 99) [DharmaNexus]. SuttaCentral records five modern translations across five languages [SuttaCentral].
